caseno: Death Reference No. 56 of 2003 with Criminal Appeal No. 2140 of 2003 with Jail Appeal No. 361 of 2003 with Jail Appeal No. 497 of 2003.
lawyer:
Md Mozammel Huq, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Iqbal Hossain, Assistant Attorney-General with Mahfuza Begum, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State Respondent. 
Md Abul Bashar, Advocate, State Defence Lawyer—For the Condemned Prisoner (Moinuddin). 
MC Chowdhury, Advocate—For the Appellant (Harun).
parties:
Moinuddin & ors ------ Condemned Prisoner.
Vs.
State ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
3. The prosecution case, as it transpires from the evidence of the informant PW 1 Abul Hossain, in short, is that on 5-3-1995 at about 4-00 PM his uncle (now deceased) Abdul Motlib sent him to the market, who after completion of marketing at about 9-30/10-00 PM came to his uncle's house and took seat in the kitchen of that house and was exchanging words with his uncle, aunt and sisters, when he heard a sound of firing from the north side of his uncle's house and since then after 10 minutes he heard a sound of kick at the door of his uncle Abdul Motlib (now deceased) and then he saw accused Moinuddin, Mofiz and Farid entered into the room of his uncle and at that point of time Farid told to Moinuddin to open fire, on that, accused Mofiz switched on his 3 battery torchlight at his uncle and accused Moinuddin fired by his gun on the right side of the chest of his uncle Abdul Motlib who fell down being injured and died within 10 minutes. On hearing hue and cry as well as sound of firing surrounding people and relatives namely, A Latif, Fatema Begum and Lutfor Rahman came there and saw his uncle's dead body and heard about the occurrence. It has been further alleged that at the time of going to Thana (Police Station) he (informant) came to know that the miscreants also shot at Abdul Hoque member by gun causing injury on his person and thereafter, when he reached nearby the house of Shamser Chairman, he further heard a sound of firing. It has been further alleged that out of previous enmity with regard for giving evidence against the accused persons in a dacoity case, they became inimical to Abdul Motlib (uncle of the informant) and accordingly, in a pre-arranged plan they committed the crime. 

 7. After closure of the evidence, the condemned prisoner and others including the appellants were examined on dock under section 342 of the CrPC, to which they repeated their innocence and declined to adduce any evidence. 

 9. Mr Md Abul Basher, the learned State Defence Lawyer appearing for the condemned prisoner, has placed before us the FIR, charge sheet, deposition of witnesses, postmortem report and other materials on record including the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence and then assails the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence on various grounds. The learned State Defence Lawyer submits that in fact, the impugned judgment so far the death penalty imposed upon the condemned prisoner based on the evidence of partisan and interested witnesses namely PW 1 Abul Hossain, PW 2 Rubi Begum, PW 3 Fatema, PW 4 Zesmin Begum, PW 5 Foiz Uddin, PW 8, Nazma Begum and PW 9, Abdur Rob whose conduct appears to be suspicious, inasmuch as the so-called eye-witnesses deposed inconsistently as to the murder of deceased Abdul Motlib. Besides, their testimonies were not corroborated by any independent witness. The learned State Defence Lawyer, after placing the post mortem report, submits that the doctor found 6(six) marks of injury on the person of deceased Abdul Motlib but from the testimony of the eye-witnesses namely, PW 1 Abul Hossain, PW 2 Rubi Begum, PW 3 Fatema, PW 4 Zesmin Begum and PW 5 Foiz Uddin, it appears that all these witnesses categorically testified in one voice that the condemned prisoner Moinuddin fired at the chest of deceased Abdul Motlib by his gun in which Abdul Motlib being injured died but the evidence of these eye-witnesses does not corroborate the post mortem report with regard to the injuries as found on the person of the deceased victim Abdul Motlib. Finally, the learned State Defence Lawyer submits that in view of the surrounding facts and circumstances and the evidence on record the death penalty in question is too severe and harsh and which deserves reduction if at all the conviction is maintained by this Court. 

 10. Mr MC Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the convict appellant Harun in Criminal Appeal No. 2140 of 2003, submits that the appellant was not named in the FIR, police at the instance of the vested quarter falsely implicated him in this case and submitted charge sheet against him without any legal basis. The learned Advocate, in the course of his argument, has taken us to the deposition of witnesses and then submits PW 1, PW 2, PW 3, PW 4, PW 5, PW 8, PW 9, PW 10, PW 11, PW 12, PW 14, PW 15, PW 16, PW 17 and PW 20 in their respective testimony did not disclose the name of the appellant Harun. The learned Advocate further submits that PW 6, PW 7 and PW 13 in their respective evidence disclosed the name of Harun but none of them disclosed any act of this appellant in the alleged occurrence. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence, so far it relates to the appellant Harun, in fact, is based on no legal evidence and, as such, at any ratio the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence so far it relates to the appellant Harun is liable to be set aside. 

 11. Mr Md Mozammel Huq, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet which was, according to him, correct, just and proper. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, in the course of his argument, has taken us through the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 27-5-2003 and other evidence on record and then submits that PW 1, PW 2, PW 3, PW 4, PW 5 and PW 8 in their respective evidence categorically testified that after kicking the door on 5-3-1995 at 10-00 PM the condemned prisoner Moinuddin and others illegally entered into the house of Abdul Motlib, at that accused Farid Ali told to Moinuddin to fire and then Mofiz switched on his torchlight and condemned prisoner Moinuddin fired at the chest of Abdul Motlib who, being injured, died within 10 minutes from the occurrence. He further submits these witnesses in lengthy cross-examination were unshaken with regard to the occurrence of killing Abdul Motlib and, as such, the learned trial Judge rightly arrived at a finding that the prosecution has successfully proved the allegation of murder against the condemned prisoner Moinuddin and accordingly, awarded the death sentence which should not be disturbed. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that from the testimony of PW 6, it appears that on 5-3-1995 at 09-30 PM the condemned prisoner Moinuddin, accused Hashmat Ali, Harun, Habibur Rahman and Kala Chand entered into the house of Abdul Hoque and then accused Moinuddin started abusing in filthy language Abdul Hoque and at one stage he fired at the right side of the belly of Abdul Hoque and thereafter, the accused persons left the premises, and PW 12 Md Nur Hossain alias Nurai stated in his evidence that accused Habibur Rahman, Kala Chand and Manik on breaking his door illegally entered into his house with dagger, gun and they demanded money to him and at one stage accused Habibur Rahman dealt dao blows on the hand and throat of PW 12 Md Nur Hossain alias Nurai and accused Kala Chand dealt a dagger blow on the chest of PW 12 and this evidence is also corroborated by PW 13 and, as such, the learned trial Judge rightly found the accused appellants named Habibur Rahman, Harun and another guilty under sections 307/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced them thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life. The learned Deputy Attorney-General further submits that the evidence of PWs 1-5 taken together with other evidences on record clearly show that all these 4(four) convicts including condemned prisoner Moinuddin in collusion with each other in a pre-arranged plan being armed with Banduk, Dao and knife committed the crime on that fateful night as a result of which A Motlib died on the spot and 2(two) other victims namely, PW 6 Abdul Hoque and PW 12 Md Nur Hossain alias Nurai sustained serious bleeding injuries on their persons and whereupon, the learned trial Judge rightly and legally on proper assessment of the entire evidence on record passed the judgment and order of conviction and sentence, which must be affirmed. 

 12. To appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates as well as the learned Deputy Attorney-General from a correct angle, let us now examine the evidence on record adduced by the prosecution in support of the charge. 

 14. PW 2, Ruby Begum, wife of the deceased victim Abdul Motlib, stated in her evidence that on 5-3-1995 at 10-00 PM accused Moinuddin being armed with a gun along with his companions entered into their house and instantaneously accused Mofiz switched on his 3-battery torchlight on her husband and then accused Moinuddin fired pointing to her husband resulting Abdul Motlib fell down and he died within 10 minutes. This witness also stated that আমার স্বামী ইহা প্রকাশ করিয়াছিল যে, তিনি নিজেই থানায় গিয়া ঘটনার কথা বলিবেন কিন্তু ছটফট করা অবস্থায় কলমা পড়িয়া স্বামী ঘরের মধ্যে মারা যায়। কুপি বাতির আলোতে ও মফিজের টর্চের আলোতে আসামীদেরকে চিনিতে পারি। In cross-examination, she denied the defence suggestion that out of previous enmity she deposed falsely against the accused persons. This witness was cross-examined at length by the defence but nothing material could be elicited that may discredit her evidence in respect of material particulars. 

 16. PW 4, Jesmin Begum, daughter of the deceased victim Abdul Motlib, as an eye-witness, stated in her evidence that on 5-3-1995 at 10-00 PM while they were making gossip in respect of their family matters, she heard sound of kicking at the door and thereafter she saw accused Moin, Mofiz and Farid entered into their house by breaking the door when accused Mofiz switched on his 3-battery torchlight and Moin fired by his gun at the chest of her father. This witness also stated that গুলি খাইয়া আমার আব্বা বলিল, মইন আমাকে গুলি করিয়া মারিয়া ফেলিল এই কথা বলিয়া আব্বা বিছানায় পড়িয়া যায় এবং সাথে সাথে মারা যান। This witness identified the accused persons on dock. 

 18. PW 5, Foizuddin, son of deceased Abdul Motlib, as an eye-witness, corroborated the evidences of PW 1, PW 2, PW 3 and PW 4 in respect of all material particulars. This witness identified the accused Moin and Mofiz on dock. 

 21. PW 7, Md Abdul Aziz stated in his evidence that on 5-3-1995 at 9-30 PM he heard a sound of kicking at the door and soon thereafter he saw in the light of a Kupibati that accused Moin, Harun and others illegally entered into the house of his sister's husband Abdul Hoque and at one stage accused Moin fired at the belly of Abdul Hoque. This witness also identified the accused Moinuddin and Harun on dock. This witness stated in his cross-examination that আমি নিজে কোন মামলা করি নাই। আমার ভগ্নিপতি মামলা করে। কোথায় মামলা করে বলতে পারব না। আমার ভগ্নিপতি কোন কাজ করিত না। আব্দুল হক মেম্বার পেশায় চোরাকারবারী ও চোরাই মালের বাটোয়ারা লইয়া অংশীদারের সাথে গন্ডগোল হয় এবং সেই গন্ডগোলে জখম প্রাপ্ত হয় আব্দুল হক এই কথা সত্য নয়। This witness also denied the defence suggestion that after being influenced by his sister's husband he deposed falsely. 

 23. PW 9, Abdur Rob stated in his evidence that on hearing sound of firing he rushed to the house of his brother Abdul Motlib and saw his brother was lying in unconscious condition. On query, he disclosed that Moinuddin fired at him with the active help of Mofiz and Farid, who 5/6 minutes after died. This witness also stated that he saw the marks of bullet injury on the chest of his brother Abdul Motlib. This witness denied the defence suggestion that out of land dispute he falsely deposed against the accused persons. 

 24. PW 10, Constable Montaz Ali stated in his evidence that on 6-3-1995 he along with Constable Shafiqur Rahman took the dead body of Abdul Motlib to Osmani Medical College Hospital for post mortem examination. 

 27. PW 13, Abbas Uddin stated in his evidence that on 5-3-1995 at 9-00 PM accused Kala Chand came and asked about his father while he wanted to know the reasons for asking about his father, at that, accused Kala Chand told him some persons are willing to meet him. This witness also stated that he saw 4(four) persons namely, Moinuddin, Habibur Rahman, Abdur Rahman and Harun standing outside of their house. This witness further stated that sometime after people in the locality took his injured father in their dwelling house when his father told him that accused Moinuddin fired at him. This witness also stated that he came to know that the accused persons on that night also killed Abdul Motlib by gun shot and also assaulted Nur Hossain alias Nuri. This witness identified accused Abdur Rahman, Harun, Moinuddin, Habibur Rahman and Baten on dock. In cross-examination, he denied the defence suggestion that he deposed falsely. 

 32. PW 19, Hajira Begum stated in her evidence that on the date of occurrence at 9-00/10-00 PM accused Moinuddin and 4(four) others entered into their house on breaking the door and started abusing her husband Abdul Hoque (PW 6) and at one stage accused Moinuddin fired on her husband Abdul Hoque and thereafter they left the premises. This witness also stated that she took her husband to hospital for treatment. This witness further stated that as a local UP member her husband Abdul Hoque gave evidence in a dacoity and arms case against the accused persons and whereupon they became angry with her husband and for which they struck her husband by gunshot. In cross-examination she stated that সত্য নয় আসামীদের সাথে আমাদের খাস জমি সংক্রান্ত বিরোধ আছে। সত্য নয় উক্ত বিরোধের কারণে আমরা একই পরিবারের তিন জন সাক্ষী দিয়েছি। আমার স্বামীর গুলি খাওয়ার ঘটনা প্রমাণে সাক্ষ্য দিচ্ছি। সত্য নয় আমি কোন ঘটনা দেখিনি। 

 34. These are all the material evidences from the side of the prosecution on which the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet convicted and sentenced the condemned prisoner and appellants and one Kala Chand as mentioned above. 

 35. On assessment of the evidence on record, it appears to us that on 5-3-1995 at night in all three occurrences took place on the same transaction one after another by the same set of accused persons. In the first occurrence which took place at the house of PW 6 Abdul Hoque on 5-3-1995 at night 9-30 PM, PW 6, Abdul Hoque as victim of the first incident stated in his deposition that on 5-3-1995 at 9-30 PM after taking meal he and his wife were making gossip on the bed while accused Moin on breaking the door entered into his sleeping room along with Hashmat, Habibur Rahman and Kala Chand, at that accused Moin told that মাটির পোয়া আর সাক্ষী দিবেনি and instantaneously fired at his belly by gun. It also appears from the testimony of this witness that 10/15 minutes after from the occurrence he heard a sound of firing from the side of nearby Abdul Motlib's house. PW 19, Hajira Begum, wife of PW 6 Abdul Hoque, as an eye-witness to the first incident, corroborated the evidence of PW 6 in toto. 

 38. Taking all the evidence together including the testimony of 6 eye-witnesses namely, PW 1, PW 2, PW 3, PW 4 PW 5 and PW 8, it is reasonable to hold that on the fateful night in a pre-arranged plan the condemned prisoner Moinuddin with the active help of accused Mofiz, Farid by breaking the door illegally entered into the house of Abdul Motlib and fired at the chest of Abdul Motlib causing his death. 

 39. On consideration of the entire evidence and materials on record, we find that PW 6 and PW 19, PW 1, PW 2, PVV 3, PW 4, PW 5, PW 8 and PW 12 are the eye-witnesses in 3 incidents. According to these witnesses, PW 1, PW 2, PW 3, PW 4, PW 5 and PW 8 were present in the second place of occurrence and saw the entire events with regard to the murder of deceased Abdul Motlib from a close distance. The evidence of these eye-witnesses so far as the nature of injury on the person of deceased Abdul Motlib also finds support from the evidence of PW 11, Dr Md Altafur Rahman, who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased Abdul Motlib. Apart from these eye-witnesses, all other local witnesses testified that they heard or came to know that on the fateful night the condemned prisoner Moinuddin along with his companions being armed with a gun illegally entered into the house of Abdul Motlib and fired at the chest of Abdul Motlib causing his death. Furthermore, we also find several police officers, constables in this case who recorded the first information report, sent the dead body of Abdul Motlib to the morgue for post mortem examination and investigated into the case. 

 41. We have already noticed that 20 witnesses were examined in this case, of whom 6 eye-witnesses, namely, PWs 1-5 and 8, categorically testified that on the date of occurrence at about 10-00 PM the condemned prisoner Moinuddin being armed with a gun (Banduk) along with Mofiz and Harun entered into the house of deceased victim Abdul Motlib by breaking the door and soon thereafter accused Mofiz switched on his 3- battery torchlight while Moinuddin fired at the chest of Abdul Motlib, who fell down being injured and died after 10 minutes. All these eye-witnesses were cross-examined by the defence at length but their testimony remain unshaken in cross-examination in respect of the material particular as to the killing of deceased Abdul Motlib. But it is very unfortunate that the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in discarding sufficient corroborative evidence of eye-witnesses acquitted Mofiz and Farid against whom specific overt act was proved by sufficient corroborative ocular evidence. However, for the reasons best known to the concerned functionaries of the State as to why the State did not prefer any appeal against-the order of acquittal so far it relates to the accused Mofiz and Farid and hence we are constrained to say that in view of such cryptic and unintelligible judgment and also for the gross negligence of concerned Ministry including solicitor's office, the real criminals somehow managed to go unpunished after committing heinous offence of murder. 

 42. We have already noticed that at the trial, the prosecution neither exhibited any injury certificate before the trial Court nor examined the doctor to prove the injuries on the persons of PW 6 and PW 12. Furthermore, save and except PW 7 and PW 19, none of the witnesses gave evidence in support of the testimony of PW 6 and PW 12 and therefore, on this point we find substance and force in the submissions of the learned Advocates for the convict-appellants that the prosecution could not prove the charge under sections 307/34 of the Penal Code against the appellants beyond doubts. 

 44. Now, coming to the question of death sentence of the appellant Moinuddin, we find from the consistent evidence of eye-witnesses that the condemned prisoner Moinuddin being armed with a gun (Banduk) along with Mofiz and Farid by breaking the door entered into the house of deceased Abdul Motlib and soon thereafter accused Farid told to Moinuddin to open fire, on that, accused Mofiz switched on his 3- battery torchlight and Moinuddin fired by his gun at the chest of Abdul Motlib, who fell down being injured and died, although, the learned trial judge by the impugned judgment acquitted accused Mofiz and Farid from the charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code while awarded death sentence to the appellant Moinuddin. In these circumstances, we think sentence of imprisonment for life instead of death sentence will meet the ends of justice. 

 45. In the result, the Death Reference No. 56 of 2003 under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is rejected and the connected Jail Appeal No. 361 of 2003 is dismissed. The conviction against the condemned prisoner under section 302 of the Penal Code is maintained but the sentence of death is altered to imprisonment for life and Criminal Appeal No. 2140 of 2003 and Jail Appeal No. 497 of 2003 are allowed, inasmuch as we have already noticed that as per the evidence on record the charge under sections 307/34 of the Penal Code was not proved beyond doubts against the appellants. Consequently, the order of conviction and sentence under sections 307/34 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet is set aside. The appellants Habibur Rahman, son of Ibrahim Ali and Harun, son of late Rushan Ali are acquitted from the charges as levelled against them. The appellant Habibur Rahman, son of Ibrahim Ali be set at liberty forthwith, if not wanted in connection with any other case. The appellant Harun is already on bail granted by this Court and hence, in view of his acquittal, he is now discharged from his bail bond.
